intel_summary.summary: US stocks were mixed-to-lower on Friday Nov 13: the S&P 500 fell 0.4% but gained 2.5% on the week, and the Nasdaq composite fell 0.9%. Nvidia slid again after CEO Jensen Huang resigned and HSBC downgraded the stock; it is on course for its worst week since January 2025, with results due late Tuesday Nov 17. Apple hit a record high as investors moved away from AI names. October PPI came in softer than expected, but rate-hike expectations remain (BofA now sees hikes at the next three Fed meetings), and a strong dollar coincided with Bitcoin falling below $70k and ether below $2k. The EIA raised its Brent forecasts again, while the IEA reported that observed global oil inventories rebounded in October. Key data next week: October CPI and Existing Home Sales (exact days not confirmed in the sources).
